messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: spike in 5xxs for eu-west region; cross-region steering showing >20% of eu requests routed to us-east. initial alert at 13:02 UTC :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: acknowledged, paging eu oncall (Priya K). oncall-bot: Priya K is oncall (shift start 12:30 UTC)
Jamie L: seeing it too, dashboards show latency + error increase starting ~12:58 UTC. traffic heatmap: a chunk from eu-west hitting us-east and failing TLS auths.
Priya K: grabbing it. assigning triage. any recent routing policy changes?
Marco R: I pushed a steering policy tweak to promote weight to eu-west yesterday for canary traffic (PR #4521). It was targeted, but I did a policy export and it looks like the fallback rules got reordered.
Sasha T: can you paste the diff?
Marco R: sure:
```diff
- fallback: [region:us-east, region:eu-west]
+ fallback: [region:eu-west, region:us-east]
```
Marco R: I think that reordering + a recent DNS cache extension means some clients are resolving to us-east while steering still prefers eu-west, causing mismatch and TLS SNI checks to fail on upstream.
Jamie L: confirmed in logs: 502s with "unexpected SNI" and backend rejecting because cert region mismatch. sample log:
```
2026-03-14T12:59:03Z ERROR request_id=abcd1234 route=steer-eu client_ip=35.192.12.45 backend=us-east tls_error="sni mismatch" status=502
```
Priya K: immediate mitigations?
Sasha T: two options: 1) revert policy change (quick) 2) force static pin for affected customer prefixes or lower DNS TTL to accelerate correct resolution. I'd do revert + temporary static pinning.
netops-bot: Suggested runbook: rollback-steering-policy -> clear prefix cache -> reduce DNS TTL to 30s -> monitor 15m.
Priya K: ok Marco, can you roll back the steering PR? post the revert id. also i'll open a DNS short-ttl for eu zone.
Marco R: rolling back now. running command:
```
redwoodctl routing apply --policy=canary-steer --rollback-to=commit:7f4c2b
```
Marco R: applied. waiting for propagation.
Jamie L: clearing KV prefix cache for affected prefixes:
```
redis-cli -h kv-cache.prod del prefix:eu:customer:*
```
Sasha T: reduced DNS TTL for eu-west steering record to 30s via cloud-dns GUI and api. command: `gcloud dns record-sets transaction start && ...` (done).
Priya K: note: customers impacted: 12k requests/min, error rate peaked 18%. creating incident ticket INC-2026-1873 and linking customer-facing alert draft.
Jamie L: posting status update to status.redwood.com draft: "We detected routing inconsistency causing intermittent errors for some EU traffic. Mitigation in progress; rolling back steering policy and lowering DNS TTL. More updates in ~15m."
Priya K: assigning oncall handoff plan: I'm primary until 14:30 UTC; if unresolved, hand to Jamie.
Sasha T: monitoring graphs: requests to us-east from eu prefix dropped 70% after rollback started. 502s decreasing.
netops-bot: telemetry: eu-west -> us-east cross-region traffic rate: before 12:58 ~2.1k/min; peak misroute 13:05 ~8.4k/min; 13:22 down to 1.6k/min.
Marco R: confirmed revert commit 7f4c2b completed at 13:15 UTC.
Jamie L: verifying TLS handshakes now show correct SNI. quick curl check for a sampled customer endpoint:
```
curl -I -H "Host: customer-a.prod.redwood" https://eu-west.example.api --resolve eu-west.example.api:443:52.19.12.3
```
response headers show cert CN=*.eu.redwood.internal -> good.
Priya K: customer impact assessment: estimated affected customers: 14 orgs with higher-error spikes; internal SLO breached for 16 minutes for eu region. drafting RCA notes.
Sasha T: opening follow-ups: 1) fix steering policy validation to ensure fallback order invariants; 2) add a safety guard on publish if DNS TTL > 60s for region weight changes; 3) improve canary to watch TLS SNI mismatch metric.
Marco R: yes I'll own 1 and 2. will add pre-publish check and an automated rollback trigger if mismatches exceed threshold.
incident-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2. created incident channel: #incident-2198765432 (auto).
Jamie L: audience update sent at 13:28 UTC. customers notified via support tickets with suggested workaround (flush local DNS).
Priya K: handing off notes before stepping out at 14:30: rollback applied, DNS TTL lowered, KV cache cleared, error rates dropping but not fully back to baseline. if error rate stalls >5% above baseline for 10m, escalate to network-runbook and call infra lead.
Jamie L: taking lead now. I'll coordinate final verification and postmortem.
Sasha T: logs attached to INC-2026-1873: link: https://internal.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-1873/logs
Marco R: quick postmortem bullets: root cause likely a publish-time reordering bug in the steering serializer + stale DNS entries; mitigations we did: revert, TTL reduction, cache clears. next: add validation and improve canary metrics.
Jamie L: thanks everyone. closing loop in 45m with final numbers and RCA draft. :white_check_mark:
